title: Ordinances for the Prince and the People

questions.question: What is the rule for the gate of the inner court that faces east on the six working days?
options: It shall be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened
It shall be open continuously to all
It shall be shut forever because the Lord entered it
It shall be opened only for the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:1 (ESV): "The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened."

questions.question: Where does the prince stand while the priests offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings?
options: By the post of the gate (inside the inner court gate facing east)
Before the bronze altar with the priests
In the outer court with the people
In the Most Holy Place
questions.correctAnswer: By the post of the gate (inside the inner court gate facing east)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:2 (ESV): "The prince shall enter by the vestibule of the gate from outside, and shall take his stand by the post of the gate. The priests shall offer his burnt offering..."

questions.question: What must the prince do before going out of the gate after worshiping at its threshold?
options: He shall go out, but the gate shall not be shut until evening
He must wash his hands and feet
He must pronounce a blessing on the people
He must fast until sundown
questions.correctAnswer: He shall go out, but the gate shall not be shut until evening
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:2 (ESV): "He shall bow down in worship at the threshold of the gate. Then he shall go out, but the gate shall not be shut until evening."

questions.question: Where do the people of the land worship the Lord on the Sabbaths and on the new moons?
options: At the entrance of that same gate (the east inner gate) before the Lord
Inside their own homes
On the mountains of Israel
In the holy chambers of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: At the entrance of that same gate (the east inner gate) before the Lord
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:3 (ESV): "The people of the land shall bow down at the entrance of that gate before the Lord on the Sabbaths and on the new moons."

questions.question: What is the required burnt offering the prince offers to the Lord on the Sabbath day?
options: Six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish
A bull without blemish
Two male goats
Twelve pigeons
questions.correctAnswer: Six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:4 (ESV): "The burnt offering that the prince offers to the Lord on the Sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish;"

questions.question: When the people of the land come before the Lord at the appointed feasts, what is the rule regarding the gates they use?
options: He who enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and he who enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate
He must enter and exit by the east gate only
He must repent at all four gates before entering
He is forbidden from entering any gate
questions.correctAnswer: He who enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and he who enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:9 (ESV): "When the people of the land come before the Lord at the appointed feasts, he who enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate; and he who enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate: no one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead."

questions.question: Why must a person not return by the same gate they entered during the feasts?
options: "No one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead" (Symbolizing progressing forward/order in the massive crowds)
To confuse the enemies of Israel
Because the gates are only one-way
To avoid seeing the prince face-to-face
questions.correctAnswer: "No one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead" (Symbolizing progressing forward/order in the massive crowds)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:9 (ESV): "...no one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead." (This implies orderliness and moving forward, not turning back after approaching God).

questions.question: If the prince makes a freewill offering (either a burnt offering or peace offerings), what must happen to the inner east gate?
options: The gate facing east shall be opened for him, and after he leaves it shall be shut
It remains open for seven days
A new gate shall be constructed for him
He must pay a tax in gold
questions.correctAnswer: The gate facing east shall be opened for him, and after he leaves it shall be shut
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:12 (ESV): "When the prince provides a freewill offering... the gate facing east shall be opened for him... Then he shall go out, and after he has gone out the gate shall be shut."

questions.question: What daily offering is required morning by morning?
options: A lamb of a year old without blemish for a burnt offering to the Lord, along with a grain offering of one sixth of an ephah and a third of a hin of oil
A bull for a sin offering
A handful of incense on the golden altar
Two loaves of showbread
questions.correctAnswer: A lamb of a year old without blemish for a burnt offering to the Lord, along with a grain offering of one sixth of an ephah and a third of a hin of oil
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:13-14 (ESV): "You shall provide a lamb a year old without blemish for a burnt offering to the Lord daily; morning by morning you shall provide it. And you shall provide a grain offering with it morning by morning, one sixth of an ephah, and a third of a hin of oil..."

questions.question: If the prince makes a gift out of his inheritance to one of his sons, to whom does it belong?
options: It shall belong to his sons; it is their property by inheritance forever
It must return to the prince in the Year of Jubilee
It is given to the priests
It is given to the poorest tribe
questions.correctAnswer: It shall belong to his sons; it is their property by inheritance forever
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:16 (ESV): "If the prince makes a gift to any of his sons out of his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons. It is their property by inheritance."

questions.question: If the prince makes a gift out of his inheritance to one of his servants, what happens to it?
options: It shall be his to the year of liberty (Jubilee), and then it shall return to the prince
The servant keeps it forever
It becomes the possession of the Levites
The servant must buy it first
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be his to the year of liberty (Jubilee), and then it shall return to the prince
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:17 (ESV): "But if he makes a gift out of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his to the year of liberty. Then it shall revert to the prince; surely his inheritance belongs to his sons, and happens to them."

questions.question: What is the prince forbidden from doing regarding the inheritance of the people?
options: He shall not take any of the inheritance of the people, thrusting them out of their property; he shall give his sons inheritance from his own property
He must not tax them more than a tenth
He must not intermarry with the common people
He must not enlist them for his personal guard
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not take any of the inheritance of the people, thrusting them out of their property; he shall give his sons inheritance from his own property
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:18 (ESV): "The prince shall not take any of the inheritance of the people, thrusting them out of their property. He shall give his sons their inheritance out of his own property, so that none of my people shall be scattered from his property."

questions.question: Ezekiel is brought by the man to the holy chambers for the priests at the extreme western end. What does the man show him there?
options: A place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so they do not bring them out to the outer court
A vault filled with gold
A hidden pool of living water
A secret armory for the Temple guards
questions.correctAnswer: A place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so they do not bring them out to the outer court
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:19-20 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, in order not to bring them out into the outer court and so transmit holiness to the people.'"

questions.question: The man then brings Ezekiel to the outer court and shows him a small court in each of the four corners (40 by 30 cubits). What are these for?
options: These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people
Prisons for those who violate the law of the sanctuary
Storage bins for the grain tithes of the people
Holding pens for the sacrificial animals
questions.correctAnswer: These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 46:21-24 details the four small corner courts with fireplaces/boiling places. (v24: "These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people").

questions.question: Why were the sacrifices of the people boiled in the outer court rather than the inner court?
options: To provide a place for the people to participate in the fellowship (peace) offerings which they were allowed to eat, separate from the priests' holy food
Because the inner court altar was only for burnt offerings, not eating
Because the smell would defile the Most Holy Place
Because there was no fire permitted in the inner court
questions.correctAnswer: To provide a place for the people to participate in the fellowship (peace) offerings which they were allowed to eat, separate from the priests' holy food
questions.explanation: The distinction is maintained between the "holy chambers" where priests ate the holy offerings (46:20) and the "outer court" kitchens where the Levites ("ministers of the temple") boiled the sacrifices of the common people for them to eat (peace offerings).

key_verse_text: "When the people of the land come before the Lord at the appointed feasts, he who enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate; and he who enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate: no one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead."
